ch01.en: This chapter is the vocabulary of the road: the names of its parts (carreggiata, corsia, banchina…), the types of roads and vehicles, and your basic duties as a driver. Learn these words well: every other chapter uses them.
tips: carreggiata = carriageway (where cars drive) · corsia = lane · banchina = verge
Many questions show a road picture: count the carriageways and lanes carefully.
Tap any Italian word to see what it means.

ch02.en: Danger signs (segnali di pericolo) are red-bordered TRIANGLES. They warn you that a danger is coming, so you slow down and pay attention. Outside towns they are usually placed about 150 m before the danger.
tips: Triangle with red border = danger ahead: slow down, be ready.
«preannuncia» = warns of in advance · «il segnale raffigurato» = the sign shown
Look carefully at the picture inside the triangle: the quiz often names the wrong danger.

ch03.en: Prohibition signs (segnali di divieto) are mostly ROUND with a red border. They tell you what you must NOT do: enter, overtake, turn, go faster than a limit, park, stop… A red diagonal bar usually means the end of the ban.
tips: Round with red border = something is forbidden.
Check WHO the ban is for: all vehicles, or only trucks, cars, motorbikes…

ch04.en: Mandatory signs (segnali di obbligo) are BLUE CIRCLES with white symbols. They tell you what you MUST do: go in a direction, keep to one side, use snow chains, keep a minimum speed… A red diagonal bar means the obligation ends.
tips: Blue circle = you must do it.
A blue square sign is information, not an obligation.

ch05.en: Priority signs (segnali di precedenza) tell you who goes first at a junction: STOP, Give way (the upside-down triangle), priority road (yellow diamond), and the signs that warn you of them. These signs are among the most asked in the exam.
tips: STOP = stop completely, then give way. Give way = slow down, stop only if needed.
«dare precedenza» = give way · «diritto di precedenza» = right of way
Yellow diamond = you are on a priority road.

ch15.en: Overtaking (il sorpasso) means passing a vehicle that is going in your same direction. In Italy you normally overtake on the LEFT, and only when you can see that the road is clear and long enough. The exam loves tricky places where it is forbidden: bends, hill tops, level crossings, pedestrian crossings and solid lines.
tips: Watch the small words: sempre (always), solo (only), anche se (even if).
Tap any Italian word to see what it means.
